title: Throughput SLA plain‑language summary, measurement rules, and crediting playbook for Dedicated
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: produce a single, plain‑language SLA definition for Dedicated throughput guarantees together with an operational measurement methodology, error budget accounting rules, and example contract text customers can sign. This ticket consolidates legal, product, and SRE inputs into a concise playbook that can be embedded in customer contracts and support runbooks.
background: Customers buying Dedicated pools ask for predictable throughput and a clear remediation path when variability occurs. Current internal drafts are either too technical for legal or too vague for SREs. We need a version that (1) is actionable for ops, (2) defensible in contract negotiations, and (3) transparent to customers on how credits are calculated.
proposed_sla_terms: Summary (plain language): For each Dedicated commitment, Redwood guarantees a delivered throughput floor measured at the commitment level over a rolling monthly window. If delivered throughput falls below the committed throughput by more than the allowable degradation threshold, Redwood will issue service credits according to the credit schedule below. Key points: (a) Guarantee is measured at a 95th percentile over the month for per-customer request throughput normalized to committed units; (b) Short transient dips shorter than 10 minutes per occurrence are excluded unless cumulative unavailability exceeds the error budget; (c) Credits are capped at the monthly committed spend. Example numeric template: Commit: 100k tokens/min sustained. Guarantee: 95th percentile delivered >= 95k tokens/min. Degradation threshold: 5% margin. Credit trigger: delivered < 95k for the monthly 95th percentile. Crediting: 10% service credit for first tier, 25% for second, 50% cap for extreme sustained failures. Detailed tiers in contract language section.
measurement_methodology: Metric definition: 'Delivered Throughput' = total successfully served token-seconds per minute normalized by committed capacity units. Measurement granularity: 1m buckets, aggregated and stored for 13 months. Statistical rule: compute the per-minute delivered throughput series, take the monthly 95th percentile value. Baseline normalization: measurements exclude planned maintenance windows that were notified per contract and capacity intentionally reserved for customer bursts that exceed committed shape. Edge cases: preemptible/spot-backed augmentation is allowed but is reported separately; if a customer purchased non-preemptible reserved units, preemptible augmentation does not count toward the guaranteed delivered throughput. Data sources: serving telemetry, billing meter, autoscaler logs. Auditability: logs and calculation scripts archived in the customer's contract-folder for 6 months after incident; calculation reproducible by SRE and legal on request.
error_budget_policy: Error budget window: monthly. Error budget = committed_throughput - delivered_throughput_95th. Allowable burn: up to 5% mitigation budget (operational variance) before credits apply. Multiple incidents within a month accumulate against the same error budget. If cumulative burn > 5% but <= 15% then Tier 1 credit applies; >15% but <=50% Tier 2 applies; >50% Tier 3 applies (caps at 50% credit). Credits are prorated to the customer's monthly Dedicated invoice. Non-credit remediation (operational actions) includes prioritized capacity allocation, canary rollouts, and temporary autoscale uplift. Customer may elect accelerated remediation which pauses error budget accrual for the duration of remediation work if joint postmortem is agreed.
remediation_playbook: Detection: Automated monitor alerts when per-customer 95th percentile projection falls below threshold with a 1-hour lookahead. Triage: SRE team runs pre-flight checks (AZ reachability, cluster health, kernel failure rates, GPU draining, network egress errors). Customer comms: notify within 30 minutes for P0 SLA breaches and provide cadence every 2 hours until recovery. Mitigations: (1) Fast-failover to warmed spare pool if configured; (2) Autoscale policy override to force short burst capacity for 20 minutes; (3) Fallback to compatible lower-latency model variant to preserve throughput if customer consents. Post-incident: joint postmortem submitted within 5 business days with root cause, corrective actions, and credit computation worksheet.
autoscale_interop: Policy interplay: Dedicated autoscaling may be configured with two controls: 'Guaranteed floor' (minimum non-preemptible units) and 'Burst ceiling' (max burstable units, may include preemptible). For SLA calculations only non-preemptible guaranteed units count toward the delivered throughput guarantee unless contract explicitly includes preemptible augmentation. Autoscaler cooldowns and startup latency: we recommend default warmup hysteresis of 180s for GPU-backed pools; any customer-requested lower hysteresis that increases risk of short instability will be flagged and excluded from SLA coverage. Autoscale override: Redwood can temporarily increase committed capacity to remediate but credits still computed against original commitment unless both parties agree an amendment.
contract_language_snippets: Plain-language snippet for customer contract: 'Redwood guarantees that the Delivered Throughput for the customer's Reserved Capacity will meet or exceed the Commitment Level at the 95th percentile over each calendar month, subject to the exclusions and measurement rules in Appendix A. If Redwood fails to meet the guarantee, the customer will receive service credits calculated as a percentage of the monthly Dedicated invoice, according to the Credit Schedule. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for throughput degradation, except as otherwise set forth in a separate support agreement.' Technical addendum snippet: 'Appendix A - Measurement and Credit Calculation: DeliveredThroughput is computed from serving telemetry with 1-minute granularity. The 95th percentile is computed over the calendar month. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer-induced throttling, and pre-notified capacity operations.' Include sample credit table: (a) >5% and <=15% shortfall => 10% credit; (b) >15% and <=50% => 25% credit; (c) >50% => 50% credit (max).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Legal has approved the plain-language and technical addendum wording; 2) SRE and billing have implemented a reproducible calculation notebook and it runs on replay data for the last 6 months; 3) Customer-facing FAQ and support runbook drafted; 4) Example contract appendix inserted into template and reviewed by Sales; 5) Two example credit calculations documented for sample commitments.
notes: Keep credit schedule conservative to avoid frequent payouts during autoscaler warmup windows; build visibility into Console so customers can track delivered throughput percentile in real time. Consider optional higher-tier commitments that include preemptible augmentation in the SLA for customers willing to accept lower credit caps. Coordinate with legal on language limiting credits as sole remedy and on regulatory exceptions.
customer_examples: Example 1: Customer A commits 200k tokens/min. Over month, 95th percentile delivered = 182k tokens/min (9% shortfall) => Tier 1 credit 10% applied to Dedicated invoice. Example 2: Customer B commits 50k tokens/min. Delivered 95th = 20k tokens/min (60% shortfall) => Tier 3 credit 50% but capped at monthly Dedicated invoice amount. Calculation worksheets must be attached to the incident record.
next_steps: 1) Schedule workshop with Legal, SRE, Billing, and Sales (owner: Marcus Chen) to finalize wording by 2025-02-24; 2) Implement calculation notebook in telemetry repo and run backtest by 2025-02-28; 3) Draft Console UI mock that surfaces 95th percentile and active error budget by 2025-03-07; 4) Prepare two customer contract amendments for pilot accounts by 2025-03-15.
